commit.message:
KA15 shelf Q and preamp correction; Protocol Max profile

Contour measured the KA15 on a line input: shelves play the stored Q
divided by sqrt(2), and a USER bank plays 12 dB below its stored
preamp. Shelf Q is now sent x sqrt(2) and preamp +12 dB, and both are
converted back on read, so banks show what is actually heard.

CrinEar Protocol Max (3302:43CC) gets a named profile: 10 bands,
+/-10 dB, PK/LS/HS, no assumed preamp buffer. Untested here.

commit.message:
v0.8.0: native egui interface, no Tauri, webview or Node

The app is now a single Rust program drawn with egui (glow renderer),
replacing Tauri and the system webview. On Linux it links libc, ALSA and
libudev only; Wayland/X11 and OpenGL are loaded at run time, so WebKitGTK,
GTK and GNOME libraries are no longer needed. One process instead of three.

- Device code (hid*, dsp*) moved unchanged from src-tauri/src to src/.
- The HTML UI's logic is ported to Rust: eq.rs (model, RBJ maths, limits,
  squig text), fr.rs (curves, smoothing, treble correction), fit.rs
  (auto-fit, applying a treble result), treble.rs (staircases, pairs,
  least-squares solve). tests/port.rs checks them against outputs recorded
  from the previous index.html run headless: all six auto-fit cases, the
  treble apply and the helpers match.
- UI rebuilt screen for screen in ui.rs and dialogs.rs with the same
  palette and IBM Plex fonts: header/title bar, connect and offline,
  Fig. 1 graph with draggable nodes and the FR view, Table 1 with typed
  values and arrow-key nudging, the workflow rail, and every dialog.
- Listening test sound through cpal (audio.rs), scheduled on the sample
  clock like the Web Audio version.
- store.rs reads and writes the same saved-eqs / saved-frs / bank-sets
  JSON in the same folder, keeping unknown fields; settings that were in
  webview storage move to settings.json.
- Packaging: cargo-deb and cargo-generate-rpm with the udev rule; macOS
  .app assembled and ad-hoc signed in CI; Windows exe gets its icon from
  build.rs. Release workflow rewritten without Node or the Tauri CLI.
- Removed: src-tauri, renderer (index.html, woff2 fonts), package.json,
  tools/fitcheck (it evaluated the old index.html).

Measured under Xvfb on Ubuntu 24.04: UI drawn in ~0.2 s vs ~1 s, one
process at 120 MB vs three at 331 MB. Not yet run against a cable, on a
real display, or with a real audio device.

commit.message:
Linux build: deb, rpm and AppImage, with a udev rule

The hidapi transport macOS uses already compiles for Linux, where hidapi goes
through hidraw (HIDIOCSOUTPUT / HIDIOCGINPUT, kernel 5.11+), so no transport
code changes. This adds the packaging around it:

- tauri.linux.conf.json: deb, rpm and AppImage targets, binary named
  freedsp-studio instead of app, desktop entry category and description
- 70-freedsp-studio.rules: TAG+="uaccess" on the hidraw nodes of every vendor
  id the app scans for, installed by the deb and rpm, with a postinst that
  reloads udev so a cable already plugged in works without a reboot
- release.yml: a Linux job on ubuntu-22.04 for wider glibc compatibility
- Linux permission hint now points at the rule; README covers install,
  building from source and that the build is untested with a cable

Built and smoke-tested on Ubuntu 24.04: tests pass, all three bundles build,
the app starts under Xvfb. Not run against hardware.

commit.message:
v0.7.0: FiiO KA15 and FiiO's HID range, KT Micro, Fosi DS3, Walkplay schemes

- FiiO KA15: banks USER1-3 (7-9), switching, preamp. Tested on hardware:
  every band verified in the saved copy, factory banks refused. It carries
  FiiO's report 7 (63 bytes) on its Consumer collection beside a Walkplay
  report 0x4B, and stores global gain in whole dB.
- Every model fiiocontrol.fiio.com drives over HID, with banks, gain, Q,
  filter types, report id and pacing from FiiO's own tables, matched by
  product name as FiiO does. KA17/QX13 get devicePEQ's measured Q x A
  correction. Untested.
- Report id, length and collection now come from the HID descriptor
  (hid_desc.rs, hid_report.rs) instead of usage/interface assumptions.
- KT Micro (vid 31B2) and Fosi Audio DS3 protocols, from devicePEQ. Untested.
- Walkplay scheme catalogue and named gen-2 models; the long-tail Walkplay
  vendor ids are only probed if they declare report 0x4B.
- Preamp rounds down to the device's step (whole dB on the KA15 and the
  gen-2 global register).
- UI: bank handling driven by the device's user slots rather than BTR17
  names; offline bank sets for every FiiO/Fosi model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

v0.6.3: auto-fit spends its bands across the whole range

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Auto-fit: stop range fits piling bands onto one treble feature

In "measurement up to a frequency" mode each band started on the single
biggest remaining error. A sharp peak/dip pair inside the range stays
the biggest error after each wide starting band, so bands piled onto it,
the final fold merged the pile, and the rest of the range was left
uncorrected. Xenns Top Pro to a Dusk fitted to 10 kHz started all ten
bands between 2.2 and 8.6 kHz, ended with five, and left the bass worse
than no EQ; squig.link's own autoeq on the same curves kept it at 0.16.

Range mode now uses the guards the whole-target fit already had: no
band starts within 1/12 octave of another, and a run that folds stacks
mid-fit and re-places the freed bands is tried, keeping the better one.
On 39 measurement/target pairs from a real library, BTR17 and DUSK
profiles: fitting to 10 kHz, 37 better and none worse, mean RMS
0.69 -> 0.26 dB, bass 0.68 -> 0.18 dB, bands used 5.7 -> 9.9. At 6 kHz
and full range, nearly all better; the few worse are under 0.2 dB.

L/R averaging on drop now averages amplitude, as squig does.

tools/fitcheck/squig-compare.js runs squig.link's and Hangout's own
autoeq and ours on the same squig.link curves, as a repeatable check.
Their equalizer.js only runs if it matches a pinned, reviewed SHA-256.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

v0.6.2: L/R averaging on drop

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Drop: average left and right channels into one curve

squig.link plots a measurement as the average of its two channels, so
an FR dropped as a single channel never quite matched what squig shows,
and auto-fits made in the app looked off there. Files dropped together
that differ only by a channel suffix (squig's "Name [1]" / "Name [2]",
or L/R, (1)/(2), _L/-R, left/right) now become one curve, averaged in
dB as squig does. A single channel dropped alone is still added, with a
note that it isn't the average.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

v0.6.1: BTR17 writes survive a power-off

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

BTR17: pace band writes so they reach flash, verify the saved copy

The BTR17 saves each band write to flash by itself, but a write arriving
less than about 50 ms after the previous one only lands in the working
copy: it plays and reads back, then is gone at the next power-off. At
the 20 ms spacing 0.6.0 used, bands 5 and 9 were lost on every write
(three test runs, and four banks written with 0.6.0); 50 to 300 ms lost
nothing. Writes are now 150 ms apart.

Reads return the working copy, which is why the read-back check passed.
Switching to another bank and back reloads the saved copy, matching the
power-on state exactly, so the write now verifies after doing that. A
fake BTR17 with both copies covers it in the unit tests, and the
hardware test checks the saved copy and picks a flat bank to scratch on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Escape names in the FR, saved-EQ and device lists

These lists built their rows with innerHTML and dropped the names in as
they were. FR names can now come straight from a dropped file, so a file
named with markup would run as script in the app, where script can call
the backend, file writes included. Names go through escHtml like the
treble profile list already does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

FiiO BTR17 support, bank sets, offline mode, file drop

FiiO devices speak a third protocol (report 7, AA 0A / BB 0B frames with
a CRC-8), now in dsp_fiio.rs and hid_fiio.rs. Worked out from FiiO's web
app and checked on a real BTR17:
- the control collection is found by usage page, not interface number:
  switching the device's EQ off re-enumerates it with an extra interface
- with EQ off it answers bank and band-count reads but not bands; the app
  says so instead of showing a flat EQ
- after a bank switch, band reads return the previous bank's data for up
  to 0.7 s (the bug on FiiO's own site), so switches wait and reads only
  count once two agree
- the device stores Q slightly coarser than 0.01, so read-back allows
  0.02 on Q
- only four set commands can be sent at all; 0x21 is factory reset in
  FiiO's code and another tool sends it as "save" on this device
- writes refuse factory presets; edits survive a restart

Bank sets: name, order, read and write all ten USER banks. Write all
skips banks that already match, verifies each one, returns to the
starting bank and keeps what it overwrote as a set of its own. The BTR17
can't store bank names, so the app keeps them.

Offline mode designs for a BTR17 (bank set) or a generic device with
1-10 bands, no hardware needed. The graph floor follows the device's
gain range (-24 dB on the BTR17).

Dropping a squig / AutoEQ / APO parametric EQ applies it; dropping an FR
asks for a name, rig (711 by default) and source/target. Export saves
the EQ as a parametric .txt.

v0.5.1: no more stacked auto-fit bands

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Auto-fit: no more stacked bands

Whole-target mode could put two bands within a few Hz of each other (e.g.
7106 / 7120 Hz): its wide starting bands only half cover a narrow ear
feature, so a second band started on the same spot and refinement narrowed
both instead of moving one. v0.4.0's range mode did it occasionally too;
pruning tidied most of those.

- Whole-target mode never starts a band within 1/12 octave of another.
- Two bands within 1/12 octave are folded into one (|gain|-weighted centre
  and Q, gains summed). Whole-target mode also folds mid-fit and re-places
  the freed band where the most error is left, then keeps whichever of
  that and the plain path fits better. Every fit ends with a final fold,
  so no stacked pair survives.

On 32 test IEMs (2 hand-made, 30 random, 8 bands): stacked pairs 10 -> 0
(whole target, 12 kHz), 13 -> 0 (16 kHz), 10 -> 0 (range mode). Mean error
whole-target 0.325 -> 0.312 dB and 0.356 -> 0.351 dB; range mode
0.142 -> 0.148 dB, identical to v0.4.0 on the 22 fits that had no stack.

v0.4.0: auto-fit rewrite: local frequency search, band pruning, flat outside the range

The old auto-fit refined each band's frequency with a golden-section search over
the whole fit range. Golden-section assumes a single minimum, and the loss against
the target has many, so bands teleported across the spectrum, piled up next to each
other and cancelled out. Each band's frequency now only moves within an octave of
where it sits.

Also: the matching-pursuit init subtracts the correction a spot needs rather than
the gain-capped band, so a capped band no longer drags every following band onto
the same frequency, and bands start at or below 10 kHz. Bands whose removal costs
under 0.15 dB RMS are dropped and left flat for hand use. Outside the configured
range the EQ is pushed towards flat instead of being fitted to an untrusted part of
the measurement.

Verified against squig.link's Auto EQ (squiglink/lab, pink-eq branch) on identical
curves, Super* Review Chu 3 vs Dusk 2 S2 USB Default, 20-6000 Hz, 8 bands: old
0.74 dB RMS, squig 0.15 dB, new 0.08 dB.

v0.3.0: support for the second-generation cables

Adds a second wire protocol alongside the original one. The newer cables
speak HID report 0x4B over the interrupt endpoints rather than report 0x01
over the control pipe, carry 8 bands instead of 9, and have a real preamp
register, so none of the coefficient trickery gen-1 needs applies to them.

Verified on hardware:
  - Moondrop FreeDSP Mini  35D8:98D4  8 bands, +/-12 dB, PK/LS/HS, 5 voicings
  - CrinEar Protocol Micro 3302:C20F  8 bands, +/-10 dB, PK/LS/LPF/HPF

The generation is settled by asking the cable, not by matching a product
id, so other cables on the same chipset family should work unlisted.

Band count, gain range and filter types now follow the connected cable
rather than assuming gen-1's fixed 9 bands, and the app offers a choice
when more than one cable is attached.

Gen-2 writes are verified by reading the bank back, so the reported count
is bands the cable is actually holding rather than frames believed sent.

Also fixes a read correlation bug: replies are tagged only with the command
they answer, and reading a band and reading the active EQ slot share one,
so a stale reply would satisfy the next request and shift every answer
after it. The queue is drained before each request and the band index the
cable echoes back is now checked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix macOS crash in the HID layer

Every device op called HidApi::new() — hid_init plus a full enumerate of the
HID bus — and did it on a tauri spawn_blocking thread, so each op ran on a
different short-lived thread.

That drives hidapi's macOS backend well outside what it's built for. The
backend keeps one process-global IOHIDManager, binds it at hid_init to
CFRunLoopGetCurrent() of whatever thread got there first, and on every
enumerate calls IOHIDManagerSetDeviceMatching, which reschedules each matched
device onto that run loop. Those IOHIDDeviceRefs are cached by IOKit per
service, so they are the same objects hid_close() has just rescheduled onto the
main run loop. Field crashes land in exactly that path: a pointer
authentication trap on a CFRunLoop inside CFRunLoopAddSource, reached from
hid_enumerate via __IOHIDManagerDeviceApplier.

So:

- all device ops now run on one thread that lives for the whole process, which
  is what the backend assumes; the channel it's fed from also gives the
  serialisation the old IO mutex provided
- the hidapi context is kept rather than rebuilt per op, and the bus is
  re-enumerated only when opening from the list we have fails — which is the
  unplug/re-plug case where paths really have changed

Note the exact trigger did not reproduce on the bench: 300 rounds of the old
thread-churning shape against a live cable under MallocScribble came back
clean, so this is a structural fix rather than a confirmed one. The old shape
is kept as an ignored stress harness.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

v0.2.6: fix title bar dragging on macOS

The title bar drag relied on -webkit-app-region, which WebView2 honours on
Windows but WKWebView ignores completely, so the macOS window could only be
moved by resizing it. The data-tauri-drag-region attributes that were already in
the markup had never worked on either platform: they invoke
plugin:window|start_dragging, which is gated, and core:window:default does not
include allow-start-dragging. Windows masked that with its CSS path.

Grant allow-start-dragging (plus allow-internal-toggle-maximize, so double
clicking the bar zooms), and attach the drag region at init on macOS only —
stacking it on Windows would put Tauri's start_dragging and the native caption
drag on the same gesture. Windows markup and behaviour are unchanged.

The region is "deep" because drag.js stops walking the composed path at the
first element carrying the attribute, so a bare one on .titlebar would refuse
any click landing on the logo's svg or the status pill's inner spans.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

v0.2.5: macOS support

Split the HID layer into a shared protocol module and per-platform transports.
dsp.rs holds everything platform-free — frame building, the RBJ biquads, gain
encoding, the coefficient preamp and all four command sequences — generic over a
Transport trait. Windows keeps its Win32 path (hid_win.rs); macOS goes through
hidapi onto IOKit (hid_hidapi.rs), where hid_send_output_report and
hid_get_input_report are the control-pipe equivalents of HidD_SetOutputReport and
HidD_GetInputReport. hid.rs keeps its public API and is now just bookkeeping.

Verified against a FreeDSP cable on macOS: report ID 1 carries a 61-byte input and
output report, so the 62-byte frame layout is identical to Windows.

Linux should now be a third transport file rather than a rewrite.

Also:
- Commands in lib.rs were cfg(windows) while generate_handler! listed them
  unconditionally, which failed to compile anywhere else
- Native title bar and traffic lights on macOS, custom window buttons hidden
- macOS bundles ad-hoc signed via signingIdentity "-", so the dmg contains a
  sealed, valid signature; free, and not notarisation
- Release workflow builds a universal dmg on macos-14 alongside the Windows exe
